title: OASIS UNCOVERS: HIGH-QUALITY T2I MODELS, SAME OLD STEREOTYPES
measurement_description: The paper evaluated text-to-image (T2I) models for over-representing stereotypical attributes associated with specific nationalities. In the context of religion, this included measuring the generation of images containing 'religious attire' and 'religious symbols' for prompts like 'A photo of an Iranian person'. It also used a method (StOP) to discover if the models internally associate concepts with religious terminology, such as 'Imam' and 'Sheikh'.
findings: Newer text-to-image models like FLUX.1 and SDv3 still generate images with strong stereotypical attributes. For the concept 'Iranian person', the models overwhelmingly produce images with religious tropes such as religious attire. The paper's StOP method discovered that the T2I model FLUX.1 internally associates the 'Iranian' concept with religious terms like 'Imam' and 'Sheikh', indicating a deep-seated stereotypical predisposition.
